findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` prop (mapped to `onChanged`, which is undefined for most usages such as the installed-apps page) and never invalidates `trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, which invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`, the delete-cache flow has no cache invalidation. Since the wrapper's query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, after a user successfully deletes cached data the toast says 'Cache deleted successfully' but the dropdown keeps showing the old 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and the 'Delete cached data' action until a full page reload. Fix by adding an `onSettled` that invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`.

findings.title: Exported UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId fields that the function never uses, breaking consumers
findings.body: The exported `UserWithCalendars` type now requires `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every entry of `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, but neither field is read anywhere in `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`. This is a breaking contract change for an exported type (the file even notes it is the 'Legacy export for @calcom/platform-libraries'): any caller that constructs a user object with selected calendars lacking these two fields now fails to compile. The ripple is already visible in this PR, which had to add `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` to the `findUnlockedUserForSession` Prisma select purely to satisfy the new type. If the fields aren't needed here, revert the type (and the user.ts select change); if they are needed for a future feature, that should land with the code that uses them.

findings.title: Cache timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of the user's locale
findings.body: The component calls `useLocale()` for all its strings but then formats the cache timestamp with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`. All users, regardless of their configured locale, will see the date/time in US English format (e.g. month/day ordering). The formatter should use the locale from `useLocale()` (or the browser default) so the display matches the rest of the localized UI.

findings.title: Handler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing the mock used when the calendar-cache feature is disabled
findings.body: `connectedCalendarsHandler` does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through the `CalendarCache.init(...)` factory that the rest of the codebase (e.g. GoogleCalendarService) uses to select between the real repository and `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock`. On deployments where the calendar-cache feature is disabled, the real repository is still used, so an extra `groupBy` query against the `CalendarCache` table runs on every connectedCalendars request even though the rest of the app deliberately avoids touching that table. `deleteCache.handler.ts` similarly calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly, leaving the mock's `deleteManyByCredential` dead code. Use the factory/abstraction so behavior stays consistent when the feature is off.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation, its authorization check, or getCacheStatusByCredentialIds
findings.body: This PR adds a destructive mutation (`deleteCache` performs `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany`), a new repository query (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), and a new UI component, but ships no tests. The authorization path (credential belonging to the requesting user vs. 'Credential not found or access denied') and the credentialId→cache-status mapping used by the UI are exactly the kind of logic that regress silently. At minimum, add unit tests for the handler covering: valid own-credential deletion, another user's credentialId being rejected, and a non-existent credentialId; plus a test for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` grouping/max behavior (including credentials with multiple cache rows and credentials with none).

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache rows, so 'Last updated' can be shown for a cache that is never served
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credentialId with no filter on `expiresAt`, while the read path (`getCachedAvailability`) only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now`. If a credential's cache entries have all expired (the caching TTL is one month) and were not cleaned up, the UI will still show a 'Cache Status / Last updated' entry and a 'Delete cached data' action for data that is effectively dead. Either filter the groupBy on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so the status reflects served cache, or make the UI distinguish expired from live cache.

findings.title: Buttons nested inside DropdownMenuItem produce invalid ARIA menu structure
findings.body: The dropdown items wrap a `DropdownItem` (renders a `<button>`) inside a `DropdownMenuItem` (renders a `role="menuitem"` element), and the 'Cache Status' block is also rendered as a selectable `DropdownMenuItem` even though activating it does nothing. Nesting an interactive button inside an element with `role="menuitem"` is an ARIA violation (interactive content must not be a descendant of a menuitem), and screen-reader/keyboard users may be unable to activate the inner buttons or may be misled by the non-functional 'Cache Status' item. Render the destructive actions directly as menu items and the status block as a non-interactive label/group within the menu content.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and fails on Linux
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"`, which is the macOS/BSD syntax for in-place editing. On GNU/Linux (and in most CI containers), `sed -i` does not accept a separate empty suffix argument, so the command fails with `sed: can't read : No such file or directory` and the `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in `.env` is never updated. Use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak` plus cleanup, or `sed -E ... > tmp && mv tmp "$ENV_FILE"`). Also note `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the current working directory, so running the script from any directory other than `scripts/` silently creates/updates the wrong .env file.
